stress.name: stress
stress.description: Stress-monitoring profile for physiological time-series and task-induced variation.
stress.analysis_question: Does the monitored signal show elevated variability or altered temporal structure under stress-related conditions?

signal_roles.primary_signal: Main physiological signal used to estimate stress-related dynamics.
signal_roles.condition: Task or context label used to compare stress and baseline states.
signal_roles.covariate: Optional metadata such as participant, session, or clinical notes.

interpretation_rules.sample_entropy: Higher values may indicate greater physiological variability and reduced predictability under stress.
interpretation_rules.spectral_entropy: Broader frequency structure may indicate distributed physiological activation or challenge responses.
interpretation_rules.dfa_exponent: DFA exponent captures temporal persistence; shifts away from baseline may reflect changing regulatory dynamics.

attention.name: attention
attention.description: Cognitive attention profile for task-driven dynamics and adaptive control.
attention.analysis_question: Does the monitored signal show greater organization or flexibility when attention is engaged by the task?

signal_roles.primary_signal: Main cognitive or neural signal associated with attentional state.
signal_roles.condition: Task phase, condition, or experimental state used for comparison.
signal_roles.covariate: Optional trial-level, session-level, or participant metadata.

interpretation_rules.sample_entropy: Higher entropy can indicate flexible attention allocation and less predictable task dynamics.
interpretation_rules.spectral_entropy: Higher spectral entropy may indicate broader engagement or more distributed processing.
interpretation_rules.dfa_exponent: Changes in DFA exponent can signal different forms of temporal coordination during attentional demands.
